recipes.name: Seafood Creole
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon hot pepper sauce (such as Tabasco®)
1 pound peeled and deveined rock shrimp (thawed if frozen)
1 pound haddock fillets (thawed if frozen) - cut into bite-size pieces

steps.text: Mix together oregano, salt, white pepper, black pepper, cayenne pepper, thyme, and basil in a small bowl; set aside.
Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium heat; stir in tomato, onion, celery, green bell pepper, and garlic. Cook and stir until the onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.

Stir in chicken stock, tomato sauce, sugar, hot pepper sauce, and bay leaves. Reduce heat to low and bring sauce to a simmer. Stir in seasoning mix and simmer until the flavors have blended, about 20 minutes.
Gently stir in rock shrimp, bay scallops, and haddock; bring sauce back to a simmer and cook until the shellfish and fish are opaque, about 20 more minutes. Remove bay leaves to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Seafood Creole
raw_recipe.description: Delectable chunks of fish, rock shrimp, and scallops bask in a spicy Creole sauce. This would go great with hot cooked rice, garlic bread, a green salad, and a glass of good white wine.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was absolutely delish!! I made it for Valentine's supper tonight and it went over fabulously well with my significant other. :-) I made the recipe exactly as written like I aways do the first time and even though we both enjoyed this creole, I would do a couple of things different in the future. Firstly, the amount of hot pepper sauce was just a little bit too much heat for me...so would go down to a quarter teaspoon and put the tabasco bottle of the table for others who may need more. Then I would add at least another times as much peeled and chopped tomato, as I didn't really think there was enough. And finally, the sauce would have been better thickened up at the end with a bit of cornstarch and water. But honestly...it really was great just the way it turned out tonight even all of that said. I recommend trying it!!

Easy to make. I made the sauce the day before and added the protein prior to serving. This makes it a perfect base to have in the freezer. I thickened with a 1:1 mixture of flour and butter. I also made a nontraditional "shrimp stock", by boiling the heads from the shrimp as well as the shells in the chicken stock, prior to adding the liquid to the pot. It adds extra shrimp flavor, but keeps the silkiness of the chicken stock. This recipe is a keeper.

Made this last night and loved it. I didn't have seafood so I replaced it with chicken instead (dark meat). I didn't use the butter as suggested. I just used olive oil to sautéed the onions, peppers and celery - don't think it needs any butter. Also I used diced tomatoes instead of fresh tomatoes. I threw in the juices from the diced tomatoes. Because I didn't have chicken broth, I added water and a teaspoon of chicken bouillon (probably didn't even need to add the bouillon) but did have too add little more salt. Took only 25 minutes to cook since I threw the chicken in along with the seasoning and tomato sauce right after the veggies were sautéed. Didn't need to simmer another 20 minutes after that...veggies were soft and tender.

I didn't have a couple of the ingredients, but exchanged them for similar things. eg I used cod, jumbo prawns and crabmeat (unfortunately, artificial). Thankfully, I mixed the spices together but didn't just dump them in, just added a spoon at a time and didn't use them all. We are not heavy spicy eaters, so I left out the hot sauce and just added a pinch of crushed chilli peppers. I too, didn't use the chicken broth, but added a tad extra of the diced tomatoes with juice and a small scoop of low sodium chicken powder. It was absolutely delicious....definitely a keeper!!! Can't wait to make it for my 'old grown children" and grandchildren. I'm quite sure they will all love it.

Delicious! This turned out better than I anticipated - it was so flavorful! I improvised with what I had: vegetable stock, scallops, flounder. (I didn't have chicken stock, celery or green pepper on hand) but otherwise I included everything else (lots of garlic, onions, fresh tomatoes, tomato sauce, all the spices listed). I read some of other reviews and added a bit of corn starch to thicken it up a bit. We ate it as a stew and added some croutons. Yummy! Definitely looking forward to making this again and I would highly recommend this recipe. Next time, I'll add the missing ingredients that I didn't have this time around.

Love this recipe! I use shrimp, chicken and beef sausage and 2 cans diced tomatoes, 1 can tomato sauce. The rest is the same. I let it simmer for up to 4 hours and serve over rice with Garlic Bread. It's a winner!

This was really good and simple to throw together! I used cod instead of haddock because that’s what I had and I also added muscles, and used crushed tomatoes instead of tomato sauce. I added a bit more stock and simmered it about an hour before adding the seafood at varying times depending on their cook times. I kept the spice as listed but for us, we could have easily doubled it. Great over rice, will definitely make this again!

Really delicious and fun to make! I had a one pound bag of frozen mixed seafood from Trader Joe's in the freezer and so, searched for a recipe to use it up and voila! Came up with this lovely Creole. Hubby is not one for heat, so next time will turn that down a notch, leaving out the splash of hot sauce and although it goes against my nature, will half the cayenne. Cooking only for two, we were fine with the one pound of seafood, and it worked well keeping all the other ingredients as are in the recipe. Next time will use three pounds of seafood as recommended as I noticed that it reheats well the next day and I will also try to freeze leftovers.
Served with a side of quinoa (extra yummy) and a watermelon salad which helped to curb the heat, even for hubby. This is definitely a keeper!

Loved this. Simple and delicious. I made a few small changes, only out of necessity--I used what I had on hand: red pepper instead of green, no white pepper, no sugar, no Tabasco (used red pepper flakes instead), didn't have fresh tomatoes so I used a can of Rotele, and no fish (only had shrimp & scallops on hand). I cut down on the liquids a bit because I omitted the fish and didn't want an excess of liquid. I served it with brown rice. You can omit the butter as well; though I used it, you can seriously cut down on the fat by leaving it out & either using the oil spray to saute, or just put them in the liquids w/o sauteing. This is very healthy and tasty.

One of best recipes I have tried in a long time. Will not hesitate to make again. As my husband likes super hot I added extra heat which was a mistake on my part. As written would have been perfect. For fish I used 12 xl large shrimp, 6 scallops, 4 lobster tails, just 1 king crab leg (Costco had a seafood deal this weekend) and 1/2 lb calamari. 2 full meals and 1 very large left over lunch. Only thing I would change is that all the fish only need 10-12 minutes. Overcooked at 20

Absolutely delicious! My friends loved it! Warning... even though I halved the hot sauce and cayenne, it was still HOT! If you like big heat, this is for you! Next time I will only use 1/4 of the HOT ingredients because it was a bit too hot for me. I ate it anyway because it was SO GOOD! I also used diced tomatoes instead of the peeled and crushed tomatoes instead of the tomato sauce. I also only used 1C of chicken bouillon because someone mentioned that it was too soupy. That worked well, but I did add a little extra crushed tomatoes toward the end! I served it over white rice and it was awesome! This is a winner!
Made this for the first time, it's a great recipe, my husband and myself loved it, fortunately I doubled the recipe so plenty of leftovers. I'll be making this again.
Made rue the day before so the flavors popped. Used scallops instead of the fish
Not enough flavor for me. I used all the spices but the hot ones. I used precooked thawed seafood mix and it was cooked to perfection in just 5 minutes. Not worth the work...
What really set this off for us was the addition of Achiote paste and homemade chicken stock!

I have to say that this is a very good tasting Creole. My mother came from Cajun parents so we grew up having my mother cook Gumbo, oyster jambalaya, shrimp etouffee and shrimp creole and many other Cajun dishes. Unfortunately mom passed away and didn’t write any of her recipes down. I was thrilled to find Plain O Bobs recipe to try. I made it last night and followed it exactly as he states but used his wife’s approach since I’m old now and can’t take the heat like I use to. Instead of 1/8 teaspoon for the pepper spices I tried 1/4 and it still gave just the right amount of heat. I took someone suggestion to put the Tabasco on the table instead of adding it to the roux during cooking. My husband put several drops in his and I tasted his and thought it does give it more enjoyable flavor but once again I can’t tolerate the heat. By the way, we used whole grain brown rice and placed a small amount in the bottom of our bowls then poured the delicious seafood creole over the top. Mother always used white rice and I was worried about the brown rice maybe being to strong and interfering with the flavors but it didn’t and worked just fine. Also the rice helps to calm down the hot spices a bit. Next time I make this recipe I am going to try using a dark beer in place of the Chicken stock because I had a friend many years ago who made his creole roux with beer in it and the taste was outstanding. This recipe tasted authentic and I will make it again with company over next time. Thank you Plain O Bob.

This was so good. I did add a little cornstarch like some others said and used a can of diced tomatoes (basil, onion and garlic). I actually added a little more hot sauce as we like spicy. I made with shrimp, scallops and lump crab. Served over white rice. Will be a regular item in our house.

Made it following the recipe with scallops, shrimp and haddock fresh. The only small deviation I made was to put the hot sauce on the table & let my husband add it to his dish. I have reflux so just the red pepper was enough for me. It was delicious & will definitely be served to guests as well as family.
My family loved it. I did substitute Rotel Lime and cilantro diced tomatoes with green chiles to give it some more heat. Otherwise it was perfect
